layout.$description: Window and container geometry for the two form factors: a resizable macOS window with a menu-bar popover, and a full-screen Android activity. There are no breakpoint tokens here on purpose — the compact/expanded boundary is Tailwind's own `sm` (640px), which every phone in portrait is below and every supported macOS window is above; a second boundary beside Tailwind's is how two scales start.

main-min-w.$description: Main window minimum width (A11Y-15). Must match tauri.conf.json. macOS only — an Android activity is whatever the device is, so A11Y-15's 'everything stays reachable' has to hold well below this as well.

popover-w.$description: The macOS menu-bar popover, and the tighter of the two width constraints the shared components face: a row that fits here fits a phone.

sidebar-w.$description: Fixed nav rail width. Expanded layout only — below the `sm` boundary the nav is a bottom bar.

sidebar-half-w.$description: Half the fixed sidebar width. Bottom-centred overlays add it to the viewport midpoint so they centre inside the desktop content pane.

tabbar-h.$description: Bottom nav height on the compact layout, the counterpart to --sidebar-w. Material 3's navigation-bar height. Add --inset-bottom to it rather than baking the inset in; the gesture bar is not always present.

content-max-width.$description: Reading measure for settings and detail panes.

inset-top.$description: Display cutout / status bar. Zero on macOS, non-zero on an edge-to-edge Android activity. A token rather than a raw env() per call site because env() with no fallback resolves to nothing rather than to 0px, and silently invalidates the calc() around it.

inset-bottom.$description: Gesture bar. The bottom nav and any bottom-anchored toast must add this.
